about: Someone joins the company: what they say or do, by what they are to the one who plays (bond: kin, friend, hire, fellow, escort, stranger) and, where it shows, their manner. A line that names more of the moment is chosen over one that names less. A person's own words (Joins "..." in Kyr) are said instead.

lines.text: {Actor} is already reaching for {their} coat. 'I was going to go anyway,' {actor} says. 'Now I don't have to go alone.'
'About time,' says {actor}, and takes the heavier bag without being asked.
{Actor} looks at you a long moment, then nods. Neither of you says anything about why.
{Actor} gets up without a word and goes for {their} boots. Whatever is out there, you will face it together.
'I was hoping you'd ask,' says {actor}, grinning for the first time since you came home. 'Give me a minute to find my other boot.'
'Of course,' says {actor}, and puts a hand on your arm. 'We'll find out together.'
'Then I'm coming,' says {actor}. 'Someone has to keep you out of trouble.'
{Actor} laughs. 'I wondered how long you'd take to ask.'
{Actor} counts the coin twice, puts it away, and shoulders {their} pack. 'Where are we going, then?'
{Actor} weighs the coin in one hand, then nods. 'For that, I'll go as far as you like. Within reason.'
{Actor} takes the coin as if it were a little less than {they} [are|is] worth. 'You'll not regret it.'
'It's your money,' says {actor}, pocketing it. 'Try not to get me killed for it.'
'I was going that way,' says {actor}. 'Better two on the road than one.'
{Actor} falls in beside you without making much of it.
'Company!' says {actor}. 'There's nothing worse than a long road and nobody to complain to.'
{Actor} considers you, then the road. 'As far as it suits us both.'
{Actor} falls in beside you, keeping close.
{Actor} comes, and stays near enough to touch.
{Actor} thinks about it, then nods. 'For a while, then.'
'Why not,' says {actor}. 'It's not as if anything is keeping me here.'
